en.title: Equities reprice sharply as Treasuries absorb the shock and credit risk begins to widen
en.deck: The 20 November sell-off was not a uniform flight to cash: equities and precious metals fell, oil rose, the dollar barely moved and Treasury yields dropped. A UKMTO-reported tanker strike near Khasab and a fire that halted operations at Iraq's Hartha power station add distinct, attributed energy-security observations without proving a sustained route or regional grid disruption.
en.regime: Cross-asset risk repricing with restrictive monetary conditions
en.key_risk: An equity valuation correction could migrate into non-bank liquidity, collateral and credit funding if spreads and redemption pressure continue to rise.

pt-BR.title: Bolsas reprecificam o risco, Treasuries absorvem o choque e o crédito começa a abrir
pt-BR.deck: A venda de 20 de novembro não foi uma fuga uniforme para o caixa: ações e metais preciosos recuaram, o petróleo subiu, o dólar quase não mudou e os rendimentos dos Treasuries caíram. Um incidente com petroleiro relatado pela UKMTO perto de Khasab e o incêndio que interrompeu a usina iraquiana de Hartha acrescentam observações distintas de segurança energética, sem comprovar bloqueio prolongado da rota ou falha regional da rede.
pt-BR.regime: Reprecificação transversal de risco sob condições monetárias restritivas
pt-BR.key_risk: Uma correção das avaliações acionárias pode alcançar a liquidez de instituições não bancárias, as garantias e o financiamento de crédito se spreads e resgates continuarem aumentando.

signal_rationale.delta: The 20 November cross-asset pattern shows a broad equity decline alongside a Treasury rally, a flat dollar, falling gold and copper, and rising oil. Two event-level energy observations available before cutoff—a UKMTO-reported tanker strike near Khasab and the Hartha station fire in Iraq—add operational risk context without establishing attribution, sustained route closure or regional grid disruption.
signal_rationale.evidence: Reuters market close data; US Treasury par curve; FRED high-yield spread through 19 November; ECB Financial Stability Review of November 2026; September Treasury TIC flows.; Reuters reporting UKMTO's 21 November tanker incident; Reuters reporting the Hartha power-station fire from INA and security officials.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Equity valuation losses can affect non-bank fund liquidity, repo collateral, redemptions and bank/non-bank funding links if volatility persists.
signal_rationale.transmission: The immediate price shock is concentrated in equities, while sovereign duration remains a hedge; credit spreads, repo terms, redemptions and the operational security of Gulf shipping are observable next channels. Local electricity interruptions in Iraq should be assessed separately from global oil-flow disruption.
signal_rationale.falsifier: Rapid equity recovery, volatility normalization and stable or narrowing credit spreads without new redemption restrictions would weaken the interpretation of a broader repricing cycle.

key_constraints: The 20 November market close is the latest full global session; 21 November is a Saturday.
The US high-yield spread is available through 19 November only at the information cutoff.
Treasury TIC flows are for September and cannot establish November portfolio flows.
The B3 was closed on 20 November; no Brazilian equity close is reported for that date.
The oil-price move reflects a reported geopolitical risk premium; no new attack is inferred from prices.

The 21 November UKMTO incident is reported by Reuters; the vessel and responsible actor are unidentified, the environmental impact is unknown, and its relation to the 20 November Khasab fire report is unestablished.
The Hartha power-station fire is reported by Reuters citing INA and security officials; cause and damage extent are unknown, and pre-fire operating capacity is not a measured post-fire loss.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 2026-11-21T05:00:00-03:00. Reuters published the UKMTO tanker report at 07:57 UTC (04:57 BRT) and the Hartha fire report at 06:22 UTC (03:22 BRT), both before cutoff.
producer_checks.novelty_decision: Distinct from the three latest editions: focuses on cross-asset transmission and funding channels after the 20 November equity sell-off, rather than another semiconductor valuation, European inflation or energy-supply report.
limitations: No same-day 20 November high-yield spread was available at cutoff.
No reliable same-day global fund-flow series was available.
TIC data are one month lagged and custody-based.
The market attribution for oil reflects Reuters reporting and is not evidence of a new attack.

The 21 November tanker incident is relayed by Reuters from UKMTO; the vessel identity, actor attribution and environmental impact remain unknown, and no link to the 20 November Khasab incident is established.
The Hartha fire is reported by Reuters citing INA and security officials; the cause and damage extent remain unknown. The pre-fire operating level of about 400 MW is not a measured post-fire loss.

revision_reason: Revision 2 adds two event-level energy observations available before the 05:00 BRT cutoff: the 07:57 UTC UKMTO-reported tanker incident near Khasab and the Hartha power-station fire in Iraq. Both are attributed, their unknown causes/actors are preserved, and neither is treated as proof of a sustained Hormuz closure or regional grid failure. EN/PT-BR prose, regional map and references were updated together.
